lines.en: Not yet. Is he the tall one, a retired sailor whose jacket is always bright orange?
lines.pt: Ainda não. É o alto, um marinheiro aposentado cuja jaqueta é sempre laranja-brilhante?

lines.en: That is him. He is quite a character, someone who can talk to anyone for hours.
lines.pt: É ele. É um personagem e tanto, alguém que consegue conversar horas com qualquer pessoa.

lines.en: Then I like him already. My neighbour Clara, a retired teacher who plays the violin, is exactly like that.

lines.en: Lovely. My cousin Joe, an engineer whose hobby is photography, is shy, but he has a great sense of humour.
lines.pt: Que bom. Meu primo Joe, um engenheiro cujo hobby é fotografia, é tímido, mas tem um ótimo senso de humor.

lines.en: Is he the one you showed me in the photo, the man wearing glasses and a green scarf?

lines.en: Yes, that is him. His wife, a nurse who works night shifts, is much more talkative, though.

lines.en: Interesting. People who are quiet at first often turn out to be the kindest, in my experience.

lines.en: That says a lot about her. Describe someone who changed your life, if you can.

facts.big: noun, a/an + noun phrase (who / whose + clause),
facts.label: Descrever pessoas com detalhe
facts.sub: Aposto: Clara, a retired teacher. Com who: a teacher who plays. Com whose: Joe, whose hobby is photography.

facts.label: Aposto
facts.sub: Um aposto é uma expressão com substantivo que explica outro, entre vírgulas: My neighbour Clara, a retired teacher, plays the violin. A informação é extra; sem ela, a frase continua completa.

facts.label: Quem / que
facts.sub: Combine o aposto com who: Clara, a retired teacher who plays the violin. Isso dá ainda mais detalhe sobre a pessoa. O verbo depois de who concorda com Clara: plays, não play. Evite repetir she.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: An appositive is a noun phrase with commas.
We say “Clara a teacher”, without commas.
Whose can describe a person’s possessions.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: An appositive is a noun phrase with commas. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “Clara a teacher”, without commas. → Falso (Use commas.)
Whose can describe a person’s possessions. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: People of Brighton · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny Saturday morning in Brighton. Ida and Noah sit in a small café near the sea. Seagulls cry, and a street musician plays. They watch people walk along the pier. Every face seems to have a story. Ida likes to describe the people she knows.

“Noah, have you met Sam, the man who runs the bookstall by the pier?” says Ida. “Not yet. Is he the tall one, a retired sailor whose jacket is always bright orange?” says Noah. “That is him. He is quite a character, someone who can talk to anyone for hours.” says Ida.
